label: D2 after choosing a2 and reaching S1 (rare a2->S1 transition)
explanation: Fires only at D2, and only when the input shows that the agent chose a2 and landed in S1, i.e. a rare transition after a2. Nearly all activation mass falls inside this conjunction (recall 0.9996, mass recall ~1.0). It never fires at D1 or GO, after a1, in S2, or on common transitions (the 17 misses are weak a1->S1 common steps). About 24% of a2->S1 steps stay below threshold. Those false positives do not follow a simple rule: restricting to good==S2 raises precision to 0.87 but lowers recall to 0.82, which gives a lower F1. Magnitude looks larger on runs of consecutive a2->S1R trials and when the good state is S2, which I saw in the example windows but did not quantify. Uses observed inputs only.

issues: The core claims hold. On the dev split the unit never fires at D1 or GO (F1 0 for each phase), it essentially never fires on a1->S1 steps (precision 0.0001), and the original predicate scores test P 0.732, R 0.999, F1 0.845, mass recall 1.0, matching the report.

The claim that there is 'no simple rule' for the roughly 25% of a2->S1 steps that stay silent is wrong, because the misses are systematic. When the previous trial reached S2 and was unrewarded (prev_reward==0 & prev_state==2), the predicate covers 7293 dev steps at precision 0.043: the unit is almost always silent there. With that case removed, the rest is P 0.87 and R 0.99.

Activation also depends on the previous trial in a graded way. Previous trial S2 and rewarded: precision 0.96, recall 0.60. Previous trial S1 and unrewarded: precision 0.75. Previous trial S1 and rewarded: precision 0.64. Overall, prev_reward==1 gives precision 0.93 against 0.45 for prev_reward==0. So the unit tracks recent history, not only the current a2->S1 transition.
The good==S2 effect the other agent saw is mostly a correlate of this history effect. Precision is 0.87 with good==S2 and 0.37 with good==S1.
Excluding the previous-S2-unrewarded case lifts test F1 from 0.845 to 0.916 (P 0.852, R 0.991, mass recall 0.999). The remaining false positives look scattered and mostly have a previous trial in S1.
The label is right that the unit is gated to a2->S1 at D2. It overclaims by implying the unit fires on every such transition, and the explanation calls a systematic exception unexplained.
skeptic.revised_label: D2 after a rare a2->S1 transition, unless the previous trial reached S2 and was unrewarded
